advanced.e: Marketing reforms aim to widen market access and competition but do not guarantee a price above MSP, which depends on prevailing demand-supply conditions, making statement 2 incorrect.

chapters.title: Industry and Industrial Policy
chapters.desc: Industrial policy resolutions, MSME and Make in India

basic.q: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 laid down the basic approach to industrial development, giving primacy to which sector?
o: A mixed economy approach with a role for both public and private sectors
basic.e: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1948 envisaged a mixed economy with defined roles for both the public and private sectors.

basic.q: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into how many schedules/categories based on the role of the state?
basic.e: The 1956 Resolution classified industries into three schedules: A (state), B (state and private), and C (private).

basic.q: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is often regarded as the 'economic constitution' of India because of what?
o: It replaced the Constitution of India
It laid down the framework for industrial development within the goal of a socialistic pattern of society
It was passed by a two-thirds majority in Parliament
It dealt exclusively with foreign trade
basic.e: The 1956 Resolution is called India's 'economic constitution' as it framed industrial policy around the goal of a socialistic pattern of society.

basic.q: The New Industrial Policy was announced in which year?
basic.e: The New Industrial Policy was announced in 1991 as part of the broader LPG reforms.

basic.q: Industrial licensing in India refers to what?
o: Requirement of prior government permission/approval to set up or expand certain industrial undertakings
basic.e: Industrial licensing required firms to obtain prior government approval before setting up or expanding specified industrial undertakings.

basic.q: MSME stands for which of the following?
basic.e: MSME stands for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

basic.q: The classification of MSMEs in India is based on which two criteria under the current framework?
o: Investment in plant & machinery/equipment and annual turnover
basic.e: MSMEs are classified using a composite criterion of investment in plant & machinery/equipment and annual turnover.

basic.q: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched in which year?
basic.e: Make in India was launched in 2014 to promote India as a global manufacturing hub.

basic.q: The primary objective of the 'Make in India' initiative is to do what?
o: Promote India as a global manufacturing hub and boost domestic manufacturing
basic.e: Make in India aims to attract investment and boost domestic manufacturing, positioning India as a global manufacturing hub.

basic.q: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, 'Schedule A' industries were those industries which were
o: Reserved exclusively for future development by the State
basic.e: Schedule A industries were reserved for future development exclusively by the State.

basic.q: Which industries were reserved for the public sector under Schedule A of the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution?
o: Arms and ammunition, atomic energy, railways
basic.e: Schedule A included strategic industries such as arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railways.

basic.q: The New Industrial Policy 1991 substantially reduced the list of industries subject to compulsory industrial licensing to approximately how many broad categories at the outset?
basic.e: The 1991 policy retained licensing for only 18 industries, a list progressively reduced further in subsequent years.

basic.q: The abolition of the 'Phased Manufacturing Programme' was most relevant to which industry?
basic.e: The Phased Manufacturing Programme, which mandated increasing indigenization over time, was notably relevant to the automobile industry.

basic.q: Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in India are primarily owned by whom?
basic.e: PSUs are enterprises where majority ownership/control rests with the Central and/or State Governments.

basic.q: The term 'Navratna' status is conferred on select what?
o: Central Public Sector Enterprises with high performance/potential, granting them greater operational autonomy
basic.e: Navratna status is granted to high-performing Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), giving them greater financial and operational autonomy.

basic.q: 'Maharatna' status, a category above Navratna, is given to CPSEs based on criteria including what?
o: Small size and local operations only
Large-scale operations, strong financial performance and global presence
basic.e: Maharatna status is reserved for large CPSEs with strong financial performance and significant global operations.

basic.q: The concept of 'industrial de-licensing' refers to what?
o: Removing the requirement of prior government license/permission for setting up or expanding most industries
Restricting industries to specific states only
basic.e: De-licensing refers to removing the requirement of obtaining prior government permission to set up or expand most industries.

basic.q: Which act historically restricted the growth of large industrial houses in India before liberalization by requiring approval for expansion beyond a certain asset size?
o: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act
basic.e: The MRTP Act required large industrial houses crossing a specified asset threshold to obtain prior approval for expansion or diversification.

intermediate.q: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, 'Schedule B' industries were characterized by what?
o: Exclusively reserved for the state with no private participation
Industries in which the state would increasingly set up new undertakings while private enterprise could also supplement state effort
Reserved for foreign direct investment only
intermediate.e: Schedule B industries allowed the state to progressively establish new units while permitting private enterprise to supplement state effort.

intermediate.q: 'Schedule C' industries under the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution comprised what?
o: All remaining industries left to the private sector, subject to overall government regulation
Industries reserved exclusively for the public sector
intermediate.e: Schedule C comprised all remaining industries left to private enterprise, though subject to overall government regulation.

intermediate.q: Which of the following was a key feature distinguishing the Industrial Policy Resolution 1948 from that of 1956?
o: 1948 nationalized all industries while 1956 privatized them
1948 gave a relatively more moderate role to state control compared to the more explicit commitment to a 'socialistic pattern of society' under 1956
intermediate.e: The 1956 Resolution explicitly committed to a 'socialistic pattern of society', going further than the more moderate mixed-economy approach of 1948.

intermediate.q: One of the primary goals of 'Make in India' alongside manufacturing promotion is to do what?
o: Improve India's Ease of Doing Business ranking and attract foreign investment
intermediate.e: Make in India also seeks to improve the ease of doing business and attract higher foreign investment into manufacturing.

intermediate.q: The MSME classification criteria were revised in 2020 to include which additional parameter besides investment?
intermediate.e: The 2020 revision added annual turnover as a criterion alongside investment for classifying MSMEs.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is a rationale for classifying enterprises separately as Micro, Small and Medium?
o: To provide differentiated policy support such as credit access, subsidies, and reservation of certain products
To restrict their growth beyond a certain size permanently
To disqualify them from receiving any government support
To merge them all into large enterprises
intermediate.e: Differentiated MSME classification enables targeted policy support such as priority sector lending and other benefits based on enterprise size.

intermediate.q: The reservation of certain products exclusively for manufacture by the small-scale sector, a policy prevalent for decades, has been
o: Progressively diluted/de-reserved to allow larger enterprises to also manufacture such products
intermediate.e: Product reservation for the small-scale sector has been progressively de-reserved over the years to allow larger enterprises entry.

intermediate.q: Industrial licensing after 1991 continues to apply to certain industries mainly on grounds of what?
o: Security and strategic concerns, safety, and environmental considerations (e.g., defence, hazardous chemicals)
intermediate.e: Post-1991 licensing is retained mainly for industries involving security, strategic, safety and environmental considerations.

intermediate.q: The shift in industrial policy from 1956 to 1991 can best be described as a shift in the role of the state from what to what?
o: An active direct producer (commanding heights) to a facilitator/regulator promoting private enterprise
A regulator to a monopolist producer
A facilitator to complete withdrawal from the economy
intermediate.e: The state's role evolved from an active direct producer occupying commanding heights to more of a facilitator/regulator.

intermediate.q: The 'Maharatna' and 'Navratna' schemes for CPSEs primarily aim to do what?
o: Grant enhanced financial and operational autonomy to well-performing PSUs to help them compete globally
Merge all PSUs into a single entity
intermediate.e: These schemes grant enhanced autonomy to well-performing CPSEs to help them compete more effectively, including globally.

intermediate.q: Disinvestment of government equity in select CPSEs since the 1990s reflects what?
o: A move to reduce the fiscal burden of running loss-making/non-strategic enterprises and mobilize resources
A move to increase the number of PSUs
Rejection of any private participation in the economy
intermediate.e: Disinvestment reflects the policy goal of reducing the fiscal burden of loss-making PSUs while mobilizing resources for the government.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is an example of policy support specifically targeted at MSMEs?
o: Priority sector lending targets for bank credit and collateral-free loan schemes
Complete exemption from all taxes permanently
intermediate.e: Priority sector lending norms and collateral-free credit schemes are specific policy measures supporting MSME access to finance.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 classified industries into Schedule A (exclusive state responsibility), Schedule B (state plus private) and Schedule C (left to private enterprise). 2. Under this Resolution, private enterprise was completely barred from operating in Schedule A industries without exception. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 correctly summarizes the three-schedule classification; statement 2 is an oversimplification, as some existing private units in Schedule A areas were allowed to continue.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding the MSME classification: 1. The classification is based solely on investment in plant and machinery, without reference to turnover. 2. A composite criterion of investment and annual turnover is used to classify an enterprise as micro, small or medium, whichever is applicable. 3. The same investment and turnover limits apply uniformly to manufacturing and service enterprises under the current classification. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect since turnover is also a criterion; statements 2 and 3 correctly reflect the current unified MSME classification that removed the earlier manufacturing/services distinction.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The New Industrial Policy 1991 abolished industrial licensing for most industries barring a small reserved list. 2. It removed the MRTP Act's asset-based threshold requiring prior government approval for expansion by large industrial houses. 3. It nationalised previously private industries in the core sector to strengthen public sector dominance. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 3 is false; the 1991 policy moved away from state dominance rather than nationalising private industry, consistent with liberalization objectives.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. 'Make in India' focuses exclusively on the manufacturing sector and excludes services. 2. 'Make in India' identifies specific sectors, including manufacturing as well as some infrastructure and service-linked sectors, for promotion. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Make in India covers a broader set of identified sectors beyond core manufacturing, making statement 1 too narrow and incorrect.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding CPSE classification: 1. Navratna status grants enhanced autonomy in investment decisions to select high-performing CPSEs. 2. Maharatna status was introduced as a category with even greater financial autonomy than Navratna. 3. Miniratna is a category with autonomy greater than that of Maharatna CPSEs. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 3 is incorrect; Miniratna status involves relatively lesser autonomy compared to Navratna and Maharatna, which rank above it.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Industrial de-licensing after 1991 meant that no industry in India requires any government approval whatsoever to be set up. 2. A small list of industries continues to require industrial licences even today, mainly on account of security, strategic, environmental, or safety considerations. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as de-licensing was not universal; a small list of industries, as noted correctly in statement 2, continues to require licences.

advanced.q: The concept of 'commanding heights of the economy' associated with the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 primarily meant what?
o: Complete state ownership of all industries
State control over key/basic and strategic industries while permitting private enterprise elsewhere
Exclusive foreign ownership of core industries
advanced.e: 'Commanding heights' meant state control over key/basic and strategic industries while private enterprise operated in other sectors.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why the New Industrial Policy 1991 is considered a watershed compared to earlier industrial policy resolutions?
o: It reversed the mixed economy framework by nationalizing private enterprises
It substantially reduced the scope of industrial licensing, the reserved public sector list, and restrictions like MRTP thresholds, marking a shift towards market orientation
It introduced industrial licensing for the first time
It abolished the concept of public sector enterprises entirely
advanced.e: The 1991 policy is a watershed as it substantially reduced licensing, the reserved public sector list, and MRTP restrictions, marking a decisive shift towards market orientation.

advanced.q: The term 'sickness' in the context of Indian industry historically referred to what?
o: Chronic financial and operational non-viability of industrial units, often addressed under BIFR (Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction)
advanced.e: 'Industrial sickness' referred to chronic financial non-viability of units, historically addressed through the BIFR mechanism.

advanced.q: Which of the following was a stated objective of reserving certain industries for the Micro and Small enterprise sector historically (product reservation policy)?
o: To protect small-scale units from competition by larger enterprises in specific product lines
To eliminate small enterprises from the market
To reserve all industries for large enterprises
To disallow any government support to MSMEs
advanced.e: Product reservation aimed to protect small-scale units from competition by larger enterprises in specified product lines.

advanced.q: The dilution/removal of 'product reservation' for the small-scale sector over the years reflects a policy recognition of what?
o: Reservation had no effect on small units
Reservation, in some cases, limited the ability of small units to scale up and benefit from economies of scale/technology upgradation
All reserved products should be banned
Large enterprises should be barred from all consumer goods
advanced.e: De-reservation reflected the recognition that product reservation could limit small units' ability to scale up and modernize.

advanced.q: Foreign Direct Investment policy liberalization complementing 'Make in India' primarily involves what?
o: Raising sectoral caps and allowing automatic route entry in a larger number of sectors
Banning all foreign investment in manufacturing
Restricting FDI to only public sector units
Applying uniform 100% FDI cap restriction across all sectors without exception
advanced.e: FDI liberalization under Make in India involves raising sectoral caps and expanding the automatic approval route across sectors.

advanced.q: Which of the following industries has historically been treated differently from most others in India's industrial licensing framework due to concerns beyond pure economic efficiency?
o: Defence production and specified hazardous/strategic industries
advanced.e: Defence production and hazardous/strategic industries continue to require licensing due to security and safety considerations beyond economic efficiency.

advanced.q: A key rationale advanced for classifying enterprises by size (MSME framework) with differentiated support is what?
o: Larger enterprises need more protection than smaller ones
Smaller enterprises often face relatively greater constraints in access to credit, technology and markets, warranting targeted support
MSMEs should be discouraged from exporting
advanced.e: Differentiated support recognizes that smaller enterprises often face greater constraints in accessing credit, technology and markets.

advanced.q: Which of the following most accurately captures the shift in the public sector's role from the 1956 policy era to the post-1991 period?
o: From being the primary engine of industrialization occupying commanding heights to a more selectively deployed instrument alongside a dominant private sector role
From private-sector led to fully state-led industrialization
No substantive change occurred in the public sector's role
Public sector's role increased continuously without any moderation after 1991
advanced.e: The public sector's role shifted from being the primary engine of industrialization to a more selectively deployed instrument as the private sector's role expanded.

advanced.q: The gradual increase in FDI limits and ease of industrial entry since 1991, taken together with initiatives like 'Make in India,' primarily reflect a policy continuity aimed at what?
o: Deepening integration of Indian industry with global value chains and attracting investment/technology
Restricting industrial growth to domestic capital only
Eliminating the role of MSMEs in the economy
advanced.e: This continuity reflects an effort to deepen India's integration with global value chains and attract greater investment and technology.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Industrial Policy Resolution 1948 already envisaged a role for the state in industries of basic and strategic importance while leaving considerable scope for private enterprise. 2. The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 marked a shift towards a more expansive role for the public sector consistent with the goal of a 'socialistic pattern of society' adopted by the Indian National Congress. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements accurately trace the evolution from the moderate mixed-economy approach of 1948 to the more expansive state-led approach formalized in 1956.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The New Industrial Policy 1991 reduced the number of industries reserved exclusively for the public sector from seventeen to a much smaller list. 2. Industries such as atomic energy and railway operations continued to be treated as areas of significant state involvement even after 1991. 3. The 1991 policy abolished the concept of a reserved list for the public sector altogether. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 3 is incorrect since a reserved list, though much shortened, was retained rather than abolished; statements 1 and 2 accurately describe the 1991 policy shift.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. MSME classification prior to 2020 distinguished between manufacturing and service enterprises with separate investment ceilings for each. 2. The 2020 revision unified the criteria for manufacturing and service enterprises under a single classification framework. 3. The 2020 revision reduced the investment limits for classification as compared to the earlier framework. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 3 is incorrect; the 2020 revision raised (not reduced) the investment thresholds and added turnover limits, easing classification criteria rather than tightening them.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Industrial licensing under the pre-1991 regime was primarily intended to channel investment according to Plan priorities and prevent concentration of economic power. 2. It had no bearing on the pace or location of industrial investment in the country. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 is incorrect; industrial licensing significantly influenced investment decisions, often criticized for causing delays and misallocation.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding the evolving public-private role in Indian industry: 1. The 1956 policy envisaged the state occupying the 'commanding heights' of the economy. 2. Liberalization since 1991 has led to complete withdrawal of the public sector from the Indian economy. 3. Strategic disinvestment policy since the 1990s has aimed at reducing government's presence in non-strategic sectors while retaining a role in select strategic sectors. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 is incorrect since the public sector continues to have a significant, though reduced and more selective, presence in the economy; statements 1 and 3 are accurate.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. 'Make in India' seeks to raise the share of manufacturing in GDP and create additional employment in the manufacturing sector. 2. 'Make in India' was launched with the explicit aim of restricting foreign direct investment into Indian manufacturing. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 is incorrect; Make in India explicitly seeks to attract greater foreign investment, not restrict it.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The abolition of licensing for most industries under the 1991 policy was accompanied by simplification of procedures for setting up industrial undertakings through mechanisms like the Industrial Entrepreneurs Memorandum (IEM). 2. Industries exempt from licensing were still required to file an IEM in many cases for statistical/monitoring purposes. 3. The 1991 reforms eliminated any requirement for environmental clearances for new industrial units. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 3 is false; environmental clearance requirements under separate environmental laws continued unaffected by the industrial policy reforms.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The evolution of industrial policy in India reflects a shift from direct state control over investment decisions towards a framework relying more on market signals and competition. 2. Despite liberalization, certain sectors continue to require licences primarily due to considerations unrelated to economic competition, such as security and environmental safety. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements accurately capture the broad trajectory of industrial policy reform and the continued, narrower rationale for licensing in specific sectors.

chapters.title: Infrastructure
chapters.desc: Power, transport, telecom, and infrastructure financing

basic.q: Which source contributes the largest share to India's total installed electricity generation capacity, combining conventional sources?
basic.e: Thermal power, dominated by coal, has historically constituted the largest share of India's installed electricity generation capacity.

basic.q: Among thermal power sources, which fuel contributes the largest share of India's installed thermal capacity?
basic.e: Coal-based power plants form the bulk of India's thermal generation capacity.

basic.q: Which ministry is primarily responsible for the power sector in India?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
basic.e: The Ministry of Power oversees generation, transmission and distribution policy for the electricity sector.

basic.q: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind fall under the purview of which ministry?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
basic.e: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal ministry for renewable energy in India.

basic.q: National Highways in India are primarily developed and maintained by:
o: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
basic.e: The NHAI, under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, is the nodal agency for National Highway development.

basic.q: Which of the following organisations manages railway infrastructure and operations in India?
o: Indian Railways under the Ministry of Railways
basic.e: Indian Railways, under the Ministry of Railways, manages the country's rail infrastructure and operations.

basic.q: Major Ports in India are governed and administered mainly under the jurisdiction of the:
o: Union Government (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways)
basic.e: Major Ports fall under Union Government administration, while minor/intermediate ports generally fall under state jurisdiction.

basic.q: Which of the following is India's apex body for regulation of telecommunications?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
basic.e: TRAI is the independent regulator for the telecommunications sector in India.

basic.q: The liberalisation of India's telecom sector, allowing greater private sector participation, gained significant momentum with which policy?
basic.e: The National Telecom Policy of 1994 was a landmark step opening the telecom sector to private participation.

basic.q: Which of the following best describes 'infrastructure' in an economic sense?
o: The basic physical and organisational structures/facilities (power, transport, communication, etc.) needed for an economy's functioning
basic.e: Infrastructure broadly covers physical/organisational facilities like power, transport and communication that support economic activity.

basic.q: The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) was launched with the objective of:
o: Providing world-class infrastructure through a large multi-year project pipeline with defined investment targets
basic.e: The National Infrastructure Pipeline is a multi-year project pipeline aiming to boost infrastructure investment across sectors.

basic.q: Which of the following power generation sources is considered a renewable energy source?
basic.e: Solar power is a renewable energy source, unlike fossil-fuel-based thermal generation.

basic.q: Hydropower plants generate electricity primarily using:
o: The kinetic energy of flowing or falling water
basic.e: Hydropower converts the kinetic/potential energy of water into electricity via turbines.

basic.q: The Golden Quadrilateral, a major National Highway project, connects which four major metro cities?
basic.e: The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata via a network of National Highways.

basic.q: Which of the following is NOT typically classified as a 'social infrastructure' sector, but rather an 'economic infrastructure' sector?
basic.e: Power generation and transmission is classified as economic infrastructure, while education, health and sanitation are social infrastructure.

basic.q: In the power sector value chain, 'transmission' refers to:
o: Generation of electricity at power plants
Bulk transfer of electricity over long distances at high voltage
Final delivery of electricity to end consumers
Mining of coal for power plants
basic.e: Transmission involves carrying bulk power at high voltage over long distances, between generation and distribution.

basic.q: 'Distribution' in the power sector refers to:
o: Bulk transfer of power at high voltage over long distances
Delivery of electricity to end consumers such as households and industries at usable voltage
Extraction of raw materials for power generation
basic.e: Distribution is the final stage delivering electricity to end consumers at usable voltage levels.

basic.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'infrastructure financing'?
o: Mobilising long-term capital (debt/equity) for large infrastructure projects like roads, power and ports
Short-term working capital loans to small traders
basic.e: Infrastructure financing involves raising long-term capital for capital-intensive infrastructure projects.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Thermal power, predominantly coal-based, has historically been the largest source of installed electricity generation capacity in India. 2. Renewable energy sources (solar, wind, small hydro, biomass) have seen a rapidly rising share in India's power capacity mix in recent years. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. Thermal power remains dominant historically, while renewables have grown rapidly in recent years.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains a key structural challenge in India's power distribution segment?
o: Excess generation capacity with no demand at all
Financial losses of state power distribution companies (DISCOMs) due to factors like transmission & distribution losses and underpricing
Complete absence of private participation in generation
Lack of any regulatory authority for tariffs
intermediate.e: DISCOM financial stress, driven by high AT&C losses and tariffs not reflecting costs, is a long-standing structural issue.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. National Highways constitute a small percentage of India's total road network but carry a large share of total road traffic. 2. State highways and district/rural roads together form the bulk of India's total road length. 3. The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana aims to provide all-weather road connectivity to eligible unconnected rural habitations. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements correctly describe India's road network structure and the objective of the PMGSY scheme.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the electricity supply value chain?
intermediate.e: Electricity flows from Generation → Transmission → Distribution to reach end consumers.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Indian Railways operates one of the largest railway networks in the world under a single management. 2. Railway freight and passenger fares in India are entirely determined by market forces without any government role. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — railway fares have historically been significantly influenced by government policy, including cross-subsidisation between passenger and freight segments.

intermediate.q: The 'landlord port model', used in port sector reforms, refers to a structure where:
o: The port authority owns the port infrastructure/land while private operators handle cargo-handling operations under concession agreements
The private sector owns all port land and infrastructure
Ports are entirely state-operated with no private role
Ports are managed solely by state governments
intermediate.e: Under the landlord port model, the port authority retains ownership of land/infrastructure while private operators run terminal operations under concessions.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's telecom sector underwent significant reform through the New Telecom Policy of 1999, moving from a fixed licence fee to a revenue-sharing regime. 2. TRAI was established as an independent regulator for the telecom sector in 1997. 3. Mobile telephony overtook fixed-line telephony in terms of subscriber base only after 2010. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — mobile subscribers overtook fixed-line subscribers much earlier, well before 2010.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains why infrastructure is often said to have 'public good' characteristics justifying government involvement?
o: Infrastructure projects always yield immediate high private profits
Infrastructure often involves high capital costs, long gestation periods, and externalities/non-excludability benefiting society broadly
Infrastructure has no role in economic growth
Private firms always prefer to invest without any government support
intermediate.e: High capital costs, long gestation, and broad externalities justify government involvement in infrastructure provision.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The National Infrastructure Pipeline envisages investment across sectors like energy, roads, railways, urban infrastructure, and irrigation over a multi-year period. 2. The National Infrastructure Pipeline is implemented solely with private sector funds, with no participation of the Union or State Governments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the NIP envisages funding shared across the Centre, States and the private sector.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best describes the 'hub and spoke' model as applied in transport/logistics infrastructure?
o: A model where all traffic flows through one central node (hub) with connections radiating out to peripheral nodes (spokes), improving efficiency
A model where every location connects directly to every other location
A model exclusively used for airport security
intermediate.e: The hub and spoke model routes traffic through a central hub, improving efficiency compared to point-to-point connections.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's installed renewable energy capacity includes solar, wind, small hydro power and biomass. 2. Nuclear power is classified as a renewable energy source in India's official energy statistics. 3. Large hydropower projects above a certain capacity threshold are sometimes categorised separately from the 'renewable energy' category used for incentive schemes. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — nuclear power is a separate category, not classified as renewable energy.

intermediate.q: Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models such as BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer) are commonly used in India primarily for financing which sector?
intermediate.e: BOT and similar PPP models are widely used for highway and other infrastructure project financing in India.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) are public sector telecom operators in India. 2. Private telecom operators were allowed only after the year 2010 in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — private telecom operators entered the Indian market in the 1990s following the National Telecom Policy 1994, much earlier than 2010.

intermediate.q: The Sagarmala Programme, aimed at port-led development, primarily focuses on:
o: Port modernisation, port connectivity and coastal economic development
intermediate.e: Sagarmala promotes port modernisation, connectivity, and coastal economic development.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India has one of the largest road networks in the world by total length. 2. Expressways in India form the largest category of roads by total length, exceeding National Highways and State Highways combined. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — expressways form only a small fraction of India's road length; village/rural roads constitute the largest category.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best describes 'stressed assets' as a challenge in infrastructure financing, particularly seen in the power sector?
o: Excess profits earned by infrastructure companies
Loans to infrastructure projects turning into non-performing assets (NPAs) due to project delays, cost overruns or poor revenue realisation
Excess government subsidies to renewable energy
intermediate.e: Stressed assets refer to infrastructure loans that turn into NPAs due to project execution or revenue-realisation problems.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Coal-based thermal power plants generally have lower capital cost per MW but higher variable/fuel costs compared to solar power. 2. Solar power plants typically have higher upfront capital costs but negligible fuel/variable costs thereafter. 3. Nuclear power plants have low fuel costs but very high capital and gestation costs. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements correctly characterise the cost structures of coal, solar and nuclear power generation.

intermediate.q: Which regulatory body is responsible for fixing electricity tariffs at the central level for inter-state generation/transmission in India?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
intermediate.e: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) regulates tariffs for inter-state generation and transmission.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's power sector reforms have progressively 'unbundled' State Electricity Boards into separate generation, transmission and distribution entities. 2. This unbundling was primarily mandated by the Electricity Act, 2003. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the Electricity Act, 2003 promoted unbundling of vertically integrated State Electricity Boards.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY) scheme was aimed at the financial turnaround of debt-laden state power distribution companies. 2. Under UDAY, participating states took over a substantial portion of their DISCOMs' outstanding debt. 3. UDAY fully and permanently eliminated all financial losses of DISCOMs across India. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 overstates the outcome — DISCOM financial stress persisted even after UDAY.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was set up under a separate Act of Parliament. 2. NHAI is the nodal agency for development of National Highways under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 3. All roads in India, irrespective of category, fall under NHAI's jurisdiction. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — NHAI was established under the NHAI Act, 1988. Statement 3 is wrong, as state highways, district and rural roads fall outside NHAI's jurisdiction.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains the rationale behind India's Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) used in highway projects?
o: The government bears the full construction cost while the private party earns nothing
A mix of upfront government funding (part of project cost) and deferred annuity payments to the private developer, balancing risk between public and private parties
Complete private ownership without any government contribution
It is used only for railway freight corridors
advanced.e: HAM shares project cost between government (upfront) and the private developer (recovered via annuities), balancing risk-sharing.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's telecom sector transitioned from a fixed-licence-fee regime to a revenue-sharing regime following recommendations under the New Telecom Policy, 1999. 2. This transition was intended to reduce the financial burden on telecom operators and encourage sector growth and tele-density expansion. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the shift to a revenue-sharing regime under NTP 1999 eased operator burden and spurred growth.

advanced.q: Which of the following is an accurate distinction between 'economic infrastructure' and 'social infrastructure'?
o: Economic infrastructure (power, transport, telecom) directly supports production processes, while social infrastructure (education, health) supports human capital development
Economic infrastructure includes only banks, while social infrastructure includes only NGOs
There is no meaningful distinction between the two
Social infrastructure always yields higher direct financial returns than economic infrastructure
advanced.e: Economic infrastructure directly enables production, while social infrastructure builds human capital.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) was launched based on the recommendations of a Task Force set up by the Ministry of Finance. 2. NIP envisages infrastructure investment to be funded through a combination of the Union Government, State Governments, and the private sector. 3. NIP investment projects are restricted only to the energy sector. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — NIP spans multiple sectors, including roads, railways, urban infrastructure and irrigation.

advanced.q: A key reason cited for relatively low private investment in certain infrastructure sub-sectors (e.g., distribution) compared to generation is:
o: Politically sensitive tariff-setting and revenue collection challenges affecting distribution companies' financial viability
Excess profitability making private entry unattractive
Absence of any government policy on distribution
advanced.e: Politically sensitive tariff-setting and revenue collection issues have discouraged private investment in distribution.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's National Highways network, though a small percentage of total road length, carries a disproportionately large share of road freight and passenger traffic. 2. Rural roads under schemes like PMGSY form the largest share of India's total road length. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct, reflecting the disproportionate traffic share of National Highways and the large length share of rural roads.

advanced.q: Which of the following best describes the concept of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) used in Indian infrastructure PPP projects?
o: Government provides upfront capital grant support to make a commercially unviable but socially/economically desirable project financially viable for private developers
It is a tax imposed on infrastructure companies
It refers to gaps in infrastructure planning documents
It is a penalty imposed on delayed infrastructure projects
advanced.e: Viability Gap Funding is a capital grant that bridges the gap between a project's cost and its commercial viability.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Major Ports in India fall under Union Government administration while non-major/minor ports generally fall under State Government jurisdiction. 2. The Sagarmala Programme focuses on port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, and coastal community development. 3. India's coastline is entirely devoid of any minor/intermediate ports, having only major ports. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is clearly false — India has numerous minor and intermediate ports besides its major ports.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why 'gestation period' is a critical consideration in infrastructure project financing?
o: Infrastructure projects yield returns instantly upon investment
Infrastructure projects typically take a long time to become operational and generate revenue, creating asset-liability mismatches for financiers
Gestation period refers only to agricultural crop cycles
It has no bearing on financing decisions
advanced.e: Long gestation periods create asset-liability mismatches, as financiers often lend short/medium-term funds against long-payback projects.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's power capacity mix has historically been dominated by coal-based thermal power due to relatively assured and cheaper domestic coal reserves. 2. Renewable energy sources like solar and wind have zero variable/operating cost implications once installed, though they face issues of intermittency. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — coal's domestic availability favoured thermal dominance, while renewables have near-zero variable costs but face intermittency challenges.

advanced.q: Which of the following is a recognised limitation associated with the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model in Indian infrastructure development?
o: Complete absence of any private sector interest historically
Risk of disputes over land acquisition, cost/time overruns, and renegotiation of contracts leading to stalled projects
PPP models eliminate all financial risk for government
PPP is applicable only in agriculture
advanced.e: Indian PPP projects have often faced land acquisition disputes, overruns and contract renegotiation issues, leading to stalled projects.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Dedicated Freight Corridors are being developed by Indian Railways to segregate freight traffic from passenger traffic on key high-density routes. 2. Dedicated Freight Corridors aim to improve average freight train speed and capacity. 3. Dedicated Freight Corridors are entirely funded by private telecom companies. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is clearly false and unrelated — Dedicated Freight Corridors are railway infrastructure projects, not telecom-funded.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains the term 'tele-density' used in telecom infrastructure statistics?
o: Number of telecom towers per square kilometre
Number of telephone connections per hundred population in a given area
Total telecom sector revenue as a share of GDP
Average call drop rate in a network
advanced.e: Tele-density measures telephone connections per hundred population, an indicator of telecom penetration.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs) require electricity distribution companies to procure a certain minimum percentage of their power from renewable energy sources. 2. RPOs are mandated at the discretion of individual private consumers rather than by regulatory authorities. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — RPOs are mandated by state electricity regulatory commissions, not left to individual consumer discretion.

advanced.q: Which of the following best captures why cross-subsidisation (e.g., industrial/commercial consumers paying higher tariffs to subsidise agricultural/residential consumers) has been a contentious issue in India's power distribution sector?
o: It has no impact on DISCOM finances
It can distort price signals and burden DISCOMs' finances while affecting industrial competitiveness
It applies uniformly to all consumer categories with no differentiation
It is unrelated to electricity tariff-setting
advanced.e: Cross-subsidisation distorts price signals and burdens DISCOM finances while raising costs for industrial/commercial consumers.

chapters.title: Services Sector and IT
chapters.desc: Services sector, IT-BPM, SEZs, and tourism

basic.q: The services sector, also known as the 'tertiary sector', typically includes:
o: Trade, banking, IT, tourism, transport and other services
basic.e: The tertiary/services sector covers trade, banking, IT, tourism, transport, and various other service activities.

basic.q: In terms of contribution to India's Gross Value Added, which sector generally has the largest share among agriculture, industry and services?
basic.e: The services sector has become the largest contributor to India's Gross Value Added in recent decades.

basic.q: In the term 'IT-BPM industry' commonly used for India's information technology sector, BPM stands for:
basic.e: BPM (Business Process Management) refers to outsourced business process services, a major component of India's IT-BPM industry.

basic.q: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) was established primarily to promote:
o: Software exports through infrastructure support and single-window clearances
basic.e: STPI was set up to promote software exports by providing infrastructure, data communication links, and single-window facilitation.

basic.q: The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act in India was enacted in the year:
basic.e: The SEZ Act was enacted in 2005 and came into effect in 2006, providing a legal framework for SEZs.

basic.q: SEZs in India are primarily aimed at promoting:
o: Exports, by offering fiscal incentives and simplified regulatory procedures within designated zones
basic.e: SEZs are designated enclaves aimed at boosting exports through incentives and simplified procedures.

basic.q: Which of the following best describes India's IT industry's primary revenue source historically?
o: Software services and exports (including IT services, BPM and engineering R&D), mainly to markets like the US and Europe
basic.e: India's IT-BPM industry has been predominantly export-oriented, serving clients mainly in the US and Europe.

basic.q: Tourism in India is broadly categorised into:
basic.e: Tourism in India is broadly split between domestic tourism and international/inbound tourism.

basic.q: 'Invisibles' in India's Balance of Payments primarily refer to:
o: Services, transfers, and income flows (non-merchandise items)
basic.e: Invisibles comprise services, income, and transfers — non-merchandise components of the current account.

basic.q: Which of the following cities is widely recognised as a major hub for India's IT/software services industry?
basic.e: Bengaluru is one of India's foremost IT/software services hubs, often called the 'Silicon Valley of India'.

basic.q: The term 'tertiary sector' in the three-sector classification of an economy (primary, secondary, tertiary) refers to:
basic.e: The tertiary sector refers to services, distinct from the primary (agriculture) and secondary (industry) sectors.

basic.q: Which of the following was a key regulatory predecessor scheme to SEZs, aimed at promoting export-oriented units through duty-free zones in India?
basic.e: Export Processing Zones (EPZs) were the precursor scheme to SEZs, promoting duty-free export-oriented zones.

basic.q: India's first Export Processing Zone was established at:
basic.e: Kandla Export Processing Zone, set up in 1965, was India's (and Asia's) first EPZ.

basic.q: Which ministry administers the Special Economic Zones (SEZ) policy in India?
basic.e: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce) administers the SEZ policy framework.

basic.q: Which of the following best defines the tourism sector's categorisation in national accounts?
o: It is treated as part of the primary sector
It is generally classified within the services (tertiary) sector, given its trade, hospitality and transport-linked activities
It is part of the secondary/manufacturing sector
It is not counted in GDP at all
basic.e: Tourism, spanning hospitality, transport and trade activities, is classified within the services sector.

basic.q: Which of the following organisations promotes software/IT export infrastructure through data communication and incubation facilities under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology?
basic.e: STPI promotes software exports through infrastructure, data communication links and incubation support.

basic.q: Which of the following is generally considered a sub-segment of India's IT-BPM industry?
basic.e: India's IT-BPM industry encompasses IT services, BPM/BPO, engineering R&D, and software products.

basic.q: Which of the following best describes Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)?
o: Contracting out specific business processes/tasks (like customer support, data processing) to a third-party service provider
basic.e: BPO involves contracting non-core business processes to third-party specialised service providers.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The services sector has consistently been the largest contributor to India's Gross Value Added among the three broad sectors in recent decades. 2. The employment share of the services sector in India has always exceeded its share in GVA. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the services sector's employment share is generally lower than its GVA share, unlike agriculture, which shows the opposite pattern.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains the relatively lower employment share of the services sector relative to its GDP share in India?
o: Services sector output tends to be more capital/skill-intensive in high-value segments like IT, leading to relatively fewer workers producing higher value output
Services sector has no workers at all
Agriculture has a very high value output per worker
intermediate.e: High-value services segments like IT are relatively capital/skill-intensive, generating high output with comparatively fewer workers.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. SEZ units in India are treated as 'foreign territory' for the purposes of certain trade and tariff provisions, though they remain within India's geographical boundary. 2. SEZs were established under the SEZ Act, 2005, replacing the earlier Export Processing Zone scheme in most respects. 3. All SEZ units in India are mandatorily state government-owned and operated. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — SEZ developers/units can be private, joint-sector, or state-owned.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best describes the role of Software Technology Parks (STPs) in India's IT sector growth, particularly in the 1990s?
o: They imposed additional import duties on software exports
They provided single-window clearance, data communication links and fiscal incentives that catalysed software export growth
They restricted foreign investment in IT
They banned outsourcing of IT services
intermediate.e: STPs provided crucial infrastructure and incentives that helped India's software export industry take off in the 1990s.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the SEZ Act, 2005, units located within SEZs enjoy certain tax and duty exemptions to promote export competitiveness. 2. SEZs in India can only be set up by the Union Government and not by private developers or state governments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — SEZs can be established by private developers, state governments, or in joint ventures.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains the concept of 'invisible exports' in the context of India's services trade?
o: Physical export of goods that are difficult to see, such as small electronic components
Export of services (like IT, tourism-related receipts) and other non-merchandise items not recorded as physical goods trade
intermediate.e: Invisible exports refer to services and non-merchandise earnings, distinct from physical/merchandise trade.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's IT-BPM exports have historically been dominated by the United States and European markets as primary destinations. 2. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai and the NCR region are among India's prominent IT/ITeS hubs. 3. The Indian IT industry primarily grew due to protectionist trade policies restricting foreign IT firms' entry into India. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — India's IT industry's growth is generally attributed to skilled workforce and cost advantages amid liberalisation, not protectionism.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is an accurate description of 'medical tourism' as a component of India's tourism sector?
o: Tourism undertaken by doctors for leisure
Foreign nationals travelling to India to avail relatively low-cost, quality healthcare/medical treatment
intermediate.e: Medical tourism involves foreign patients travelling to India for affordable, quality healthcare services.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Foreign Trade Policy and SEZ framework together aim to boost India's export competitiveness. 2. SEZ units are entirely exempt from all Indian labour laws by default under the SEZ Act. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — SEZ units are not automatically granted a blanket exemption from labour laws under the central SEZ Act.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains why the services sector is sometimes described as showing signs of premature growth in India relative to industrialisation?
o: Because the industry sector grew faster than services throughout India's history

Because the services sector's share in GDP rose sharply even while the industrial/manufacturing sector's share remained relatively modest, unlike the classical agriculture-industry-services growth pattern
Because the services sector has no exports
intermediate.e: India's growth pattern saw the services sector expand rapidly ahead of a strong manufacturing base, unlike the classical development sequence.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's IT-BPM industry includes segments such as IT services, business process management (BPM), software products, and engineering R&D. 2. India has historically been among the leading global exporters of IT services. 3. India's IT-BPM sector primarily serves only the domestic Indian market with negligible export orientation. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is clearly false — the IT-BPM sector has strong export orientation.

intermediate.q: Which of the following organisations is responsible for regulating and promoting SEZs by according approvals through a Board of Approval mechanism in India?
o: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce)
intermediate.e: SEZ proposals are approved through a Board of Approval under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Foreign exchange earnings from tourism form part of India's invisible receipts in the Balance of Payments' current account. 2. Tourism-related foreign exchange earnings are recorded under the capital account of India's Balance of Payments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — tourism receipts are recorded as invisible services exports under the current account, not the capital account.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best describes 'engineering and R&D (ER&D) services' as a segment of India's IT-BPM industry?
o: Services encompassing product design, testing and engineering services offered to global clients across sectors like automotive, aerospace and telecom
intermediate.e: ER&D services involve high-value engineering, design and testing work for global clients across various industries.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's services sector encompasses a wide array of activities including trade, hotels, transport, communication, financial services, real estate, and public administration. 2. Public administration and defence services are excluded from the services sector classification in national accounts. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — public administration and defence are actually included within services sector classification.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is a commonly cited reason for India's competitive advantage in IT/software services exports?
o: A large pool of English-speaking, technically skilled workforce combined with relatively lower wage costs
intermediate.e: India's IT export competitiveness stems largely from its skilled, English-speaking workforce and cost advantages.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. SEZs are required to be a net foreign exchange earner over a stipulated period as one of the conditions for approval. 2. Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) sales from SEZ units are treated as imports into India and attract applicable customs duties. 3. SEZ developers can avail exemption from certain duties on goods/services procured for authorised operations. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements correctly describe key features of the SEZ regulatory framework.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best captures the meaning of 'inward' versus 'outward' medical tourism for India?
o: Inward refers to Indians travelling abroad for treatment; outward refers to foreigners coming to India
Inward refers to foreign patients travelling to India for treatment; outward refers to Indian patients travelling abroad for treatment
Neither term is used in tourism economics
intermediate.e: Inward medical tourism means foreign patients coming to India, while outward means Indian patients going abroad for treatment.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 provides for setting up of SEZs by the Central Government, State Governments, or private/joint sector entities. 2. Units in SEZs are exempt from routine customs examination of export/import cargo to facilitate ease of trade, though subject to overall regulatory oversight. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct, reflecting key facilitative features of the SEZ Act, 2005.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's IT-BPM industry's growth since the 1990s is closely linked to economic liberalisation, improved telecom/data connectivity, and global outsourcing trends. 2. Y2K (Year 2000) remediation projects in the late 1990s gave a significant early boost to Indian software services exports. 3. India's IT industry's growth has been entirely independent of exchange rate movements between the Rupee and the US Dollar. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — IT export competitiveness is meaningfully influenced by Rupee-Dollar exchange rate movements given dollar-denominated revenues.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The services sector's share in India's GVA has generally exceeded that of agriculture and industry combined in recent years. 2. Within services, sub-segments like financial services, real estate, trade, hotels and transport, and public administration are typically included. 3. India's services sector is a negligible contributor to the country's export earnings. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is clearly false, as IT and other services exports form a major share of India's export earnings.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why some economists caution against India's growth pattern being overly 'services-led', bypassing a strong manufacturing/industrial base?
o: Services sector generates no employment at all
Concerns that a large workforce, particularly less-skilled, may not find adequate employment opportunities in high-skill services, unlike labour-intensive manufacturing
Services sector contributes negatively to GDP
There is no such economic concern discussed by economists
advanced.e: A services-led model may not absorb India's large, relatively less-skilled workforce as effectively as labour-intensive manufacturing could.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. SEZ units are generally allowed duty-free import/domestic procurement of goods for authorised operations within the zone. 2. Sales made by SEZ units into the Domestic Tariff Area (rest of India) are treated on par with sales within the SEZ, with no import duty implications. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong — DTA sales from SEZ units are treated as imports into India and attract applicable customs duty.

advanced.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the benefits under the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) scheme from those under the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) scheme for IT units?
o: They are identical schemes with no differences

STPI historically offered scheme-based tax benefits for export-oriented software units regardless of physical zone, while SEZ benefits are tied to physical location within notified zones under a different exemption framework
SEZ applies only to the textile sector
advanced.e: STPI benefits applied to registered units regardless of location, while SEZ benefits are tied to operating within a notified physical zone.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's exports of computer services (software) constitute a major share of the country's overall services exports. 2. Travel and transportation receipts also form significant components of India's services exports/invisibles. 3. Remittances from Indians working abroad are classified as goods exports rather than as part of invisibles/current transfers. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — remittances are classified under current transfers/invisibles, not goods exports.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains the term 'net foreign exchange earner (NFE)' obligation applicable to SEZ units under Indian SEZ regulations?
o: SEZ units must ensure that foreign exchange earned through exports over a specified period exceeds foreign exchange spent on imports and other permissible outflows
SEZ units must hold foreign currency reserves equal to their total investment
NFE refers to net profit only
NFE has no relevance to SEZ approval
advanced.e: The NFE obligation requires SEZ units to be net positive earners of foreign exchange over the stipulated period.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The share of agriculture in India's workforce has historically been higher than its share in GVA, indicating relatively lower productivity per worker compared to industry and services. 2. The services sector in India generally shows the opposite pattern — a workforce share lower than its GVA share, indicating relatively higher productivity per worker in many high-value services segments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements correctly capture the contrasting productivity patterns between agriculture and high-value services segments.

advanced.q: Which of the following is an accurate description of the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS), relevant to international trade in IT/BPM services?
o: A WTO agreement exclusively on agricultural tariffs
A WTO framework covering different modes of international trade in services, including cross-border supply and movement of natural persons
A domestic Indian law on textile standards
advanced.e: GATS is a WTO agreement establishing rules and modes for international trade in services.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Mode 1 under GATS refers to cross-border supply of services, relevant to IT services delivered remotely from India to overseas clients. 2. Mode 4 under GATS refers to the temporary movement of natural persons (e.g., IT professionals) to supply services abroad. 3. GATS modes of supply are entirely irrelevant to India's IT-BPM export strategy and WTO negotiating positions. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — GATS Modes 1 and 4 are highly relevant to India's IT export interests and WTO negotiating stance.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains a key vulnerability associated with India's IT-BPM export-driven growth model?
o: Complete insulation from global economic slowdowns
High dependence on a few key export markets (like the US and Europe) and sensitivity to global demand fluctuations, protectionist visa policies abroad, and currency volatility
No dependence on external markets at all
advanced.e: Heavy reliance on a few overseas markets exposes India's IT-BPM sector to external demand shocks, visa policy changes, and currency volatility.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The services sector includes both 'market services' like trade and banking, and 'non-market services' such as public administration and defence. 2. Public administration and defence services are valued in national accounts mainly based on the cost of inputs, such as employee compensation, rather than market sale prices, since they are non-market in nature. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements correctly describe how market and non-market services are treated differently in national accounting valuation.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why ease-of-doing-business reforms (e.g., single-window clearances, simplified compliance) are considered important for both SEZ units and the wider services/IT sector?
o: They have no bearing on investment decisions
They reduce transaction costs and regulatory delays, making India more attractive for export-oriented investment including in IT/ITeS
They eliminate the need for any taxation
advanced.e: Lower transaction costs and faster clearances improve India's attractiveness for export-oriented investment, including in IT/ITeS.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Export Processing Zones (EPZs), precursors to SEZs, were set up in India starting with Kandla in 1965. 2. The SEZ Act, 2005 converted several existing EPZs into SEZs and provided a comprehensive legal framework. 3. Under the SEZ scheme, State Governments have no role whatsoever, with SEZ approvals resting exclusively with the Union Government. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — State Governments do play a role, such as recommending proposals and providing supporting infrastructure/concessions.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why IT/BPM services are sometimes described as 'weightless exports' in trade literature?
o: Because IT hardware components are physically very light
Because these exports involve intangible service delivery, often via data/electronic transmission, rather than physical shipment of goods
Because BPM companies do not generate any revenue
Because IT exports are not counted in trade statistics
advanced.e: Weightless exports refers to intangible, electronically delivered services, unlike traditional physical merchandise trade.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India's tourism sector contributes to foreign exchange earnings, employment generation, and preservation of cultural/heritage assets. 2. Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) and Foreign Exchange Earnings (FEEs) from tourism are indicators commonly tracked to assess the sector's performance. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements correctly describe the multiple benefits of tourism and the standard indicators used to track its performance.

advanced.q: Which of the following best captures a structural criticism of India's SEZ policy raised over time?
o: SEZs led to zero employment generation anywhere
Concerns about loss of agricultural land, revenue forgone due to tax incentives, and uneven regional distribution of SEZ benefits
SEZs eliminated all forms of export activity in India
SEZs are prohibited by the Constitution
advanced.e: Criticisms of the SEZ policy have centred on land acquisition issues, revenue forgone from tax incentives, and uneven regional spread of benefits.

chapters.title: Money and Monetary Policy
chapters.desc: Money functions, RBI tools, and monetary policy framework

basic.q: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
basic.e: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the provisions of the RBI Act, 1934.

basic.q: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India nationalised?
basic.e: RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 under the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.

basic.q: The Reserve Bank of India was constituted under which Act?
basic.e: RBI was set up under the RBI Act, 1934, which provides the legal basis for its functioning.

basic.q: Which function of money refers to its use in facilitating buying and selling of goods and services without the need for barter?
basic.e: Money acting as a medium of exchange eliminates the need for a double coincidence of wants required in barter.

basic.q: Money's ability to retain purchasing power over time, allowing wealth to be saved and used later, describes which function?
basic.e: The store of value function allows money to be saved now and used for future purchases without significant loss of value.

basic.q: The function of money that allows the value of goods and services to be expressed and compared in a common denomination is known as?
basic.e: As a unit of account, money provides a common measure of value for pricing and comparing different goods and services.

basic.q: Money used to settle debts that are payable in the future, such as loan repayments, illustrates which function of money?
basic.e: The standard of deferred payment function allows money to be used for settling future obligations like credit and loans.

basic.q: Repo rate refers to the rate at which?
o: RBI borrows money from commercial banks
RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities
Commercial banks lend to each other
RBI lends to the government directly
basic.e: The repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to banks against the collateral of government securities.

basic.q: Reverse repo rate is the rate at which?
o: RBI lends money to commercial banks
RBI borrows funds from commercial banks
Commercial banks borrow from the government
basic.e: The reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows surplus funds from commercial banks, absorbing liquidity from the system.

basic.q: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to the minimum percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be?
o: Kept as cash with the RBI
basic.e: CRR is the portion of a bank's net demand and time liabilities kept as cash with the RBI, on which no interest is paid.

basic.q: Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) can be maintained by banks in the form of?
o: Cash, gold, or approved government securities held by the bank itself
basic.e: SLR can be maintained in cash, gold, or unencumbered approved government securities held by the bank itself, unlike CRR which goes to RBI.

basic.q: Open Market Operations (OMO) conducted by the RBI involve?
o: Buying and selling of government securities in the open market
basic.e: OMO involves RBI buying or selling government securities in the open market to regulate liquidity in the banking system.

basic.q: The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) allows banks to borrow overnight funds from RBI by dipping into their?
basic.e: Under MSF, scheduled banks can borrow overnight funds from RBI against their SLR securities, usually at a rate higher than the repo rate.

basic.q: The Bank Rate is the rate at which RBI is willing to?
o: Lend long-term funds to banks without collateral
basic.e: The Bank Rate is the standard rate at which RBI is prepared to lend long-term funds to banks without any collateral requirement.

basic.q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) was constituted in India in the year?
basic.e: The MPC was constituted in 2016 following an amendment to the RBI Act, 1934, to institutionalise inflation targeting.

basic.q: How many total members does the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI have?
basic.e: The MPC has six members: the RBI Governor (Chairperson), two other RBI officials, and three external members appointed by the Government of India.

basic.q: Legal tender refers to money that?
o: Can only be used for international trade
Must be legally accepted for settlement of a debt or transaction
Is issued only by commercial banks
Has intrinsic commodity value equal to its face value
basic.e: Legal tender is currency that must be accepted by law when offered in settlement of a debt or transaction.

basic.q: Fiat money is money that?
o: Has value because of its metal content
Derives its value from government order/decree rather than a physical commodity
Can only be issued by the Ministry of Finance
basic.e: Fiat money has value because the government has declared it legal tender, not because it is backed by gold or any commodity.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) balances kept with the RBI earn interest for commercial banks. 2. Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) can be maintained by banks in the form of approved government securities held by the banks themselves. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as CRR balances kept with RBI earn no interest. Statement 2 is correct as SLR assets are held by banks themselves, unlike CRR which is deposited with RBI.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. An increase in the repo rate injects more liquidity into the banking system. 2. The reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI absorbs excess liquidity from commercial banks. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; increasing the repo rate makes borrowing costlier for banks and reduces liquidity rather than injecting it. Statement 2 is correct since the reverse repo rate is used by RBI to absorb surplus funds from banks.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): 1. The MPC has six members. 2. Three members of the MPC, including the Governor, are from the RBI. 3.
